question: What part inventory and naming rule do the locked checks under flightdeck/testbench/suites/_checks/ apply for spec behaviours B1 and B2 (checks part-coverage, part-coverage-selftest and the sweep-* checks)? Report: each category of part (fc subcommands from the runner's usage, hooks, role files, schemas, templates, validators, gates, workflow scripts, files distribute writes into .claude/) with the count and the full list of parts in it as the checks compute it today; exactly how a suite case is judged to "name" a part (path or subcommand token matching rules, including how case names are collected); what alteration the sweep applies per category and what counts as the case going red; where the exempt list lives and what it holds; and how many sweep chunks exist per category and which parts fall in each chunk.
answer: The B1 check (part-coverage) verifies that every part in the inventory is named by at least one case. Parts are categorized: subcommand (35: fc boundary, fc budget, fc check, fc critic render, fc distribute, fc doctor, fc events append|summary|usage, fc evidence, fc launch activate|end|escalate|gate|kickoff|land|new|note|phase|pin|status, fc lint spec, fc locked, fc plan render|write, fc report, fc return, fc runlog show|stub, fc validate, fc verifier render, fc verify, fc worker merge|render|return); hook (6: boundary-guard.mjs, event-log.mjs, lock-guard.mjs, session-end.mjs, stop-gate.mjs, structural-check.mjs); role (10: critic.md, explorer.md, implementer.md, orchestrator.md, planner.md, spec-attacker.md, spec-builder.md, spec-judge.md, test-builder.md, verifier.md); schema (10: check-result, critic-findings, event, explorer-return, launch, plan, spec, tests-map, verifier-verdict, worker-return); template (19 in templates/, including kickoff/* subdirectory); validator (8: spec-readiness-lint, validate-all, validate-kickoff, validate-launch, validate-plan, validate-return, validate-spec, validate-tests-map); gate (3: acceptance-gate, contracts-gate, structural-gate); workflow (3: fc-explore.js, fc-implement.js, fc-review.js); distributed-role (10 in .claude/agents/flightcrew/); distributed-workflow (3 in .claude/workflows/). A case names a part when its name (after removing ' [defect]' suffix) contains either: for subcommands, the space-separated tokens 'fc <command>' or 'fc <command> <sub>' bounded by non-word characters; for paths, the repository-relative path bounded by non-path-characters (matching /[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]/) [parts.mjs:110-133]. The sweep (B2) alters each part: subcommand exit codes inverted, hook decisions flipped, role 'name' frontmatter field dropped, schema top-level 'required' removed, template first slot renamed, validator/gate exit codes inverted, workflow 'export const meta' removed, distributed files altered as their source kind [parts.mjs:11-15]. A case goes red when it passes unaltered but fails after alteration; a part is held when at least one naming case goes red [sweep-run.mjs:4-6]. The exempt list lives at flightdeck/testbench/suites/_checks/fixtures/sweep-exempt.json and currently holds an empty array (no exemptions); format is JSON array of {part, reason} entries [parts.mjs:401-415]. Sweep chunks: subcommands 6 chunks (1-5 parts each, 5-6-6-6-6-6), hooks 2 chunks (3-3), roles 2 chunks (5-5), schemas 2 chunks (5-5), templates 4 chunks (4-5-5-5), validators-gates 2 chunks (5-6), workflow scripts 1 chunk (3), distributed 3 chunks (4-4-5) [computed via chunkOf function distributing sorted parts by Math.floor((i-1)*len/n) to Math.floor(i*len/n)].
